svg.title: Flower Anatomy Drag and Drop — Static SVG Learning Interface
svg.desc: A textbook-style interactive-looking SVG for learning flower anatomy. Contains a central flower diagram with arrows to target areas, a word bank of draggable-style labels, instruction panel, and hint/check/reset popups using anchor navigation and :target visibility toggles. No scripts, no images, all vectors.

g.text: 1) Study the flower diagram and the empty label slots.
2) Use the word bank to match terms to their target areas.
3) Click Hint for guidance or Check Answer to reveal placements.
A bee carries pollen to the stigma, then a pollen tube grows
down the style to the ovary where fertilization happens.
Match each word bank label to the correct slot by imagining a drag and drop. Use the buttons above for help.
Start by placing the four big ideas: Petal, Sepal, Stamen, Pistil. Then place the sub-parts:
Compare these placements with your mental matches. Close to continue exploring.
Because this is a static, script-free SVG, “Reset” simply closes any open overlays.
Use the word bank to imagine placing each label into the correct slot. Click “Check Answer” to reveal the solution overlay at any time.
1) Identify the center: Pistil (stigma → style → ovary)
3) Outside layers: Petals; beneath them: Sepals
4) Base of the flower: Receptacle connects to the stem
